sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which natural energy source is harnessed using large wind turbines?
What is the process of making yarn from raw cotton fibers called?
Which season experiences the shortest days and the longest nights in a hemisphere?
Which unique monument in India is known worldwide as a symbol of love and is made of white marble?
Which of these is considered a non-renewable source of energy?
The rotation of the Earth on its own axis causes which natural rhythm?
Which creature is known for naturally producing fine threads used to make shiny cloth?
What do we call a historical building or natural landscape that is protected for its cultural importance?
The protective layer of gases that surrounds Earth and gives us air to breathe is called the:
Which of these natural fibers is obtained by shearing the fleece of a sheep?
Briefly explain the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy sources. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Renewable sources like solar and wind replenish naturally and never run out. Non-renewable sources like coal and oil take millions of years to form and will eventually deplete.

questions.question_text: How are clothes made from raw cotton? Mention the two main steps after harvesting. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: After harvesting, raw cotton goes through spinning to create strong yarn. Then, the yarn is woven together on machines called looms to create large sheets of fabric.

questions.question_text: Why do we experience different seasons throughout the year? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: We experience different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis while it revolves around the Sun, changing the amount of sunlight each hemisphere receives.

questions.question_text: Name one unique historical monument in your country and state why it is famous. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a unique historical monument. It is famous worldwide for its beautiful white marble architecture and was built by Shah Jahan.

questions.question_text: Give two simple ways students can help protect our shared home, the Earth. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Students can protect the Earth by turning off lights when not needed to save energy and by planting trees in their neighborhood to keep the air clean.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are visiting a busy textile factory. Describe the sights and sounds of the clothes-making process around you. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I can hear the loud, rhythmic clacking of giant weaving machines called looms. Workers are busily guiding colorful threads on large spools. The air smells slightly of fabric dye, and I see long sheets of bright cloth rolling out ready to be cut and stitched.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are standing at a famous historical heritage site. Describe its ancient architecture and how it makes you feel about the past. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I am standing before a massive stone fort with tall, thick walls and beautifully carved arches. Looking at the detailed pillars, I feel amazed by the skill of ancient builders and deeply connected to the rich history of the kings who once lived here.

questions.question_text: Explain how solar energy works and why it is better for our environment compared to burning fossil fuels like coal. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Solar energy is generated by capturing sunlight using special panels that convert it directly into electricity. It is much better for our environment because it is a clean, renewable resource that never runs out. Unlike burning coal, solar power does not release harmful smoke or dangerous greenhouse gases into our atmosphere.

questions.question_text: Describe the journey of a woollen sweater, starting from the sheep on a farm to the final piece of clothing you wear in winter. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The journey begins when a farmer shears the thick fleece from a sheep. This raw wool is cleaned, combed, and spun into soft yarn at a factory. The yarn is then dyed in warm colors and knitted by machines or by hand into a cozy sweater that keeps us warm during winter.
